correctness.rationale: For all n≥7 the binary open-neighbor update is a 2×2 Laurent block over R=F₂[z]/(zⁿ−1). The determinant is z^−4 Φ₅²; at Φ₅ the trace is 1, giving comaximal lifted eigenroots and one local zero-primary free rank-one summand acted on by unit·Φ₅². Multiplication by Φ₅² over F₂[z]/Φ₅^e has exactly kernel dimension 4min(2t,e), establishing the all-n iterate rank and exact first-entrance distribution, and fixed points follow from det(B+I)=z^−4(z+1)^4Φ₅. Two independent source checkers separately verified n=7..120; exhaustive update of 2^20 Desargues states reproduced the n=10 image and fixed counts. A finite test is not treated as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2011 generalized Petersen real-spectrum article gives the two-layer spectral setup but not the characteristic-two local module, its repeated fifth-cyclotomic divisor, or exact nilpotent first-entry counts. A 2006 general prime-characteristic convolution paper supplies broad formal context, not this graph-family computation. Searches of the mathematical research index and public web, comparison with earlier parity results on distinct graph families, and inspection of the closest primary full text disclosed no result implying the full all-n theorem. Remaining historical-indexing risk is acknowledged. The argument separates statements by what they prove rather than by titles alone.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical article in binary network dynamics, Lights Out, modular adjacency algebra or a specialized generalized Petersen graph rank table could contain an equivalent result.

value.rationale: For the natural infinite cubic generalized Petersen family, the theorem gives every first-periodic-entry population, sharp maximum transient and exact fixed-space count. Squared fifth-cyclotomic resonance yields a nontrivial half-speed nilpotent clock and a sharp arithmetic distinction among 5∤n, odd multiples of five, and n=5·2^s with transient time n/10 and exponentially small periodic-state density. This is a meaningful dynamical classification rather than an isolated small computation or a renamed general finite-map consequence.
